declarations.docstring:
In a bicategory, we can compose the 1-morphisms `f : a ⟶ b` and `g : b ⟶ c` to obtain
a 1-morphism `f ≫ g : a ⟶ c`. This composition does not need to be strictly associative,
but there is a specified associator, `α_ f g h : (f ≫ g) ≫ h ≅ f ≫ (g ≫ h)`.
There is an identity 1-morphism `𝟙 a : a ⟶ a`, with specified left and right unitor
isomorphisms `λ_ f : 𝟙 a ≫ f ≅ f` and `ρ_ f : f ≫ 𝟙 a ≅ f`.
These associators and unitors satisfy the pentagon and triangle equations.

See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/bicategory.
declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Bicategory
declarations.type: Type u → Type (max (max u (v + 1)) (w + 1))

declarations.docstring:
A Reedy structure on a category `C` equipped with two multiplicative
classes of morphisms `W₁` and `W₂` consists of the data of a degree
map for objects `deg : C → α`, where `α` is a well ordered type. The first
two axioms `lt₁` and `lt₂` express the behaviour of the degree with
respect to morphisms in `W₁` (resp. `W₂`) that are not identities, and
the last axiom says that any morphism can be factored in a unique way
as a morphism in `W₁` followed by a morphism in `W₂`.
declarations.name: HomotopicalAlgebra.ReedyStructure
declarations.type:
{C : Type u_1} →
  [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v_1, u_1} C] →
    (W₁ W₂ : CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.{v_1, u_1} C) →
      [CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsMultiplicative.{v_1, u_1} W₁] →
        [CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsMultiplicative.{v_1, u_1} W₂] →
          (α : Type u_2) →
            [inst : LinearOrder.{u_2} α] →
              [OrderBot.{u_2} α] → [SuccOrder.{u_2} α] → [WellFoundedLT.{u_2} α] → Type (max u_1 u_2)

gaps.consequence: Ordinary nerves and strict Segal laws are available. No groupoid-nerve Kan result was located in the scanned directories, and its instance is absent from the selected imports. The ordinary groupoid example does not certify a Kan nerve.

SSet.RelativeMorphism is a strict relative map with a homotopy-class API. It is not the fixed-label derived MapRel or categorical MapCat required by D-RT-23. Available restriction fibrations require an explicit mono and Kan target.

Category-of-elements machinery is available. Kernel.Augmented implements incidence, explicit boundary-transport equations, lossless shape/label separation, a lawful additive-label algebra, the active-map obstruction, and strict 2-category extraction from any algebra. The reverse strict 2-category algebra, cell/hom round trips, arbitrary substitution compatibility and discrete hom nerves are checked. A relative free cell algebra over fixed vertical/horizontal incidence has a generated congruence, proved quotient laws, a universal mapping equivalence and finite term support. The explicit generating presheaf base, free vertical paths, change of base for lawful algebras and global free mapping property are checked. The reusable monad-map algebra lifting and exact-square recognition step are proved under explicit hypotheses; the generating graphs are categorically equivalent to presheaves, with elementary base density. The global algebra category, free/forgetful adjunction and induced monad are checked, with a fully faithful comparison and reconstruction of its maps preserving arbitrary substitution. Vertical categories and functors are reconstructed from arbitrary generating-monad algebras, with a natural equivalence recovering the vertical category of each existing augmented algebra. Incident cells and all primitive operations are reconstructed, with a surjective full-boundary evaluation map preserving both identities and arbitrary substitution. All five reconstructed augmented equation families and action identification are proved, yielding essential surjectivity, the comparison equivalence and monadicity. The actual free-arity nerve square, monadic restriction, canonical comparison and its compatibility with both monadic equivalences are constructed. The conditional augmented nerve theorem proves fullness and recognition under density of the supplied arities and pointwise invertibility of that specific comparison. Finite incidence supports, their filtered-colimit presentation and the equivalence between finite incidence and finite presentability are proved. A small dense candidate family of finite incidence diagrams is constructed; its nerve theorem requires canonical-comparison invertibility. The candidate's monad exactness and any required canonical geometric arity presentation, unconditional augmented nerve recognition, labelled diagram model, walking nerves, coherent Mod, and small-space classifier laws remain construction obligations (AT-FD-7 and dependent gates).
